raw_response:
I have farmed this wheat-maize land a long time, so I will not do anything too fancy. I will follow what has worked on my own field and what the better growers around me do. On 13.1 mu, fertilizer is a big cost, but if I cut too hard and the yield drops, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I have well water, so I will count on irrigation at the key times and push for a steady harvest from both crops. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, give more nitrogen at jointing, water about 3 times if the season is normal, and spray 2 times so disease and aphids do not get ahead of me. After wheat harvest, I will get the maize in quickly, mostly keep the straw handled and the ground turned lightly or seeded with little disturbance, use hybrid seed like most people do here, put part of the fertilizer early and part around the big bell-mouth stage, water 2 times if rain is not enough, and spray 2 times for weeds and insects. I will keep the rates a little on the safe side because I would rather spend some fertilizer money than lose grain.
